title: Dedicated capacity entitlement & crediting guidelines for guaranteed throughput
creator: Mei Alvarez
description: Background: As we move more customers to Dedicated capacity, commercial contracts must reflect how Redwood measures and remedies degraded throughput. This ticket captures a pragmatic, auditable way to define entitlements, compute credits when capacity promises are not met, and clarify interplay with autoscaling and maintenance. It will be the single source of truth for legal, revenue, and customer success when drafting or negotiating commitments.
proposal: Introduce an entitlement matrix + contiguous error-budget model: 1) Define a customer-facing 'Committed Throughput' in requests per second (rps) and a 95th/99th percentile latency SLO over 30-day windows for each capacity SKU. 2) Measure service-level attainment using normalized 'effective tokens per second' for multi-model fleets where token cost varies. 3) Compute monthly credits when availability of committed throughput falls below thresholds. Credits are proportional to the shortfall and capped by a maximum monthly credit percentage. 4) Autoscaling behavior: rapid autoscale events that restore capacity within a pre-defined remediation window (default 15 minutes) reduce credit scope; uncontrolled degradation beyond remediation window triggers full credit calculation. 5) Provide contract language snippets that specify measurement sources (metrics published to the customer's Console and an audit log of balancing events).
acceptance_criteria: Formal definition of 'Committed Throughput' with units and per-fleet aggregation rules
Error budget and crediting formula documented with worked examples for small and large customers
Contract boilerplate ready for legal review including exclusion clauses for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
Observability spec that lists metrics & endpoints we will publish to customers for independent verification
Runbook that ties incident severity to credit eligibility and automated credit issuance flow
measurement_definitions: We will use two correlated signals: (A) 'Provisioned RPS' = the contractual committed rps per fleet; (B) 'Observed Effective RPS' = sum over requests of (tokens_per_request / avg_token_cost_factor) measured at service ingress per minute. Attainment is computed as Observed / Provisioned per 5-minute bucket. Monthly attainment = weighted average of 5-minute buckets across the billing month, weighted by bucket request volume. Latency SLOs are computed as p95 and p99 for token-generation latency excluding cold-start windows. All measurements are derived from telemetry exported to the customer's dedicated metrics endpoint and internal audit logs; raw counters retained for 90 days for dispute resolution.
error_budget_and_crediting: Credit formula: If monthly attainment < 99.5% => credit = min( ((Provisioned - Observed)/Provisioned) * 30% * MonthlyFee, MaxCreditCap ). MaxCreditCap defaults to 50% of MonthlyFee for single-region failures or 100% for total-global outage for the fleet subject to a validated RCA. Partial credits: when degradation is restored within RemediationWindow (default 15 minutes), credit is applied pro-rata only for buckets beyond that window. Examples included: 1) Customer with 1000rps provisioned sees 950 effective rps for 12 hours in a month -> computed shortfall and resulting credit shown. 2) Impact of autoscale burst: short dips of <15 minutes are not credited if autoscale event is visible in audit log and remediation initiated. Credit issuance workflow: automated calculation pipeline -> legal validation flag for credits above threshold -> automatic application to next invoice for credits <= ThresholdCreditAmount; manual review otherwise.
contract_snippets:
1) Definition clause sample: 'Committed Throughput' means the average requests-per-second rate that Redwood guarantees for the Customer's Dedicated fleet, as specified in Exhibit A. Measurement will be performed against the Observed Effective RPS reported in the Redwood Console over the applicable measurement window.

2) Remedy clause sample: If monthly attainment falls below the Service Level, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit equal to the percentage of Monthly Fees computed as described in Schedule B. Service Credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Redwood's failure to meet the Committed Throughput.

3) Exclusions sample: No credits will be due for Degradation caused by: (a) Customer configuration changes; (b) Scheduled Maintenance where Customer received >=72 hours notice; (c) Force Majeure; (d) third-party cloud provider regional outages not caused by Redwood's misconfiguration.

4) Autoscale & remediation sample: 'RemediationWindow' means the period (default 15 minutes) following detection during which Redwood may restore committed throughput without Customer entitlement to full credits; partial credits may apply per the crediting formula.'
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers dispute measurement methodology. Mitigation: publish raw counters and a reconciliation dashboard; retention of 90-day audit logs for disputes.
Risk: Credit liability balloon for wide outages. Mitigation: cap monthly credit exposure; require legal review for credits above threshold; include SLA carve-outs for provider outages.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaling causing noisy short dips. Mitigation: RemediationWindow and automated detection of autoscale events in audit logs to avoid inappropriate credits.
Risk: Complexity for multi-model fleets with different token economics. Mitigation: normalize by effective-token-cost factor and document conversion rules per model family.
